newsitem.title: USA: Investors won't abandon stocks, fund executive says.
newsitem.headline: Investors won't abandon stocks, fund executive says.

text.p: Mutual fund investors will not be the cause of any future bear market in U.S. stocks, a top fund industry executive said Tuesday.
"I don't think it's logical to (conclude) that mutual fund shareholders will be the cause of the next bear market," Don Powell, chairman of the Investment Company Institute, said.
Powell's comments echoed the results of a Reuters survey released Monday where 61 percent of stock or mutual fund holders said they would not sell if the stock market dropped dramatically.
Asked what they would do if the market dropped dramatically, only 4 percent said they would sell their investments and get out of the market immediately, the poll showed.
Powell said he did not expect that redemptions by U.S. fund investors would lead to a bear market.
"There is no evidence of a run of mutual funds in any of the past 14 bear markets," he said.
Powell said a look at past bear markets indicated that redemptions did not increase and in some cases there was a slight increase in net new sales.

Matthew Fink, president of the Washington-based mutual fund trade group, said he expected that the Securities and Exchange Commission would propose a new shorter fund prospectus within the next month. The profile prospectus will be only two to three pages long and contain simple language to explain the basis of the fund.
